- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes in history, then drop too sharply — suggesting overshoot and premature mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after mid-period troughs — indicating lagged or delayed response to true trend.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized: model often assumes prices will return to a “central” level too quickly, ignoring persistence or structural volatility.
- Forecasts show strong bias toward higher values when history includes recent high prices — model fails to adjust downward sufficiently.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior: once a price drops, forecasts remain low for several days, even if true price rebounds — suggesting poor lag correction.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility — overreacting to short-term noise, especially in the first 10 days of the window.
